overview: This file documents Japan’s evolving system of immigration control, alien registration, labor restriction, and overseas migration between 1931 and 1939, while incorporating translations of regulations dating back to 1899. It covers metropolitan Japan, colonial Taiwan, and the South Seas Mandate; examines Chinese labor migration, foreign performers and temporary workers, alien landownership, Japanese settlement in Brazil and Manchuria, and international restrictions on Japanese migrants; and records American consular efforts to interpret and respond to Japanese policy. The collection culminates in Japan’s comprehensive 1939 ordinance governing foreigners’ entry, residence, travel, policing, and deportation.
interest: Immigration control by police discretion, Chinese laborer rules, the President Jefferson incident, and rejecting American retaliation in kind.
